identity.name: EMAIL — AiTM Session-Token Theft to Mailbox-Reconnaissance Account Takeover (Meddler-in-the-Middle)
identity.summary: An AiTM reverse-proxy phish captures the post-MFA Microsoft 365 session cookie and replays it from a new ASN — an Entra success whose MFA is satisfied by a token claim, from an ASN outside the mailbox owner's baseline. The operator then logs on to the compromised mailbox and searches finance-related mail for payment fraud. Low-signal alone; fused on user_principal they name the takeover.
identity.description: Meddler-in-the-Middle (AiTM) phishing defeats MFA by proxying the real login page: the phishing server sits between the victim and Microsoft 365, forwards credentials AND the OTP to the legitimate site, and receives a valid session cookie back (T1557 / T1539). Unit 42's meddler-phishing reporting documents this reverse-proxy tradecraft and the tokenized lure URLs (e.g. login[.]mcrsfts-passwdupdate[.]com/HMxVQmxZ) that Advanced URL Filtering blocks; per Unit 42, once the MitM server 'would receive a real session cookie from the legitimate site' the attacker 'would log on to the compromised Outlook account and continually search for finance-related emails and attachments in order to find opportunities for payment fraud'. With the stolen cookie the attacker signs in without solving MFA again (T1550.004). The specific sign-in-log signature used here — an Entra success whose MFA requirement is 'satisfied by a claim in the token', from an ASN outside the mailbox owner's baseline — is standard Microsoft 365 / Entra ID detection engineering (SRC-MICROSOFT-365-DOCS) layered on top of the source's cookie-theft finding, not a signature the Unit 42 post itself reports. The operator then monetizes the mailbox exactly as the source describes: manual logon and repeated finance-mail reconnaissance for payment fraud (T1114.002). This card is correlation-terminal (methodology family F2, Causality Stitching Validation): three per-source XQL legs — (A) a permitted click to an AiTM look-alike domain in proofpoint_tap_raw, (B) a token-replay sign-in from a new ASN in msft_azure_ad_signin, (C) post-compromise finance-mail reconnaissance on the mailbox in the Microsoft 365 unified/Entra audit (msft_o365) — are stitched by CR-EMAIL-0005 on the single join key user_principal within one incident window. Signal C on its own is routine mailbox activity; it is the co-occurrence with A+B on the same identity that names the account takeover. The AiTM domain and the anomalous ASN ride along as incident evidence.

campaigns: EvilProxy / Evilginx2 phishing-as-a-service AiTM credential + session-token theft against Microsoft 365 tenants (2021-2026)

payload.code:
# Non-destructive AiTM account-takeover chain. All hosts use the reserved
# .invalid TLD / documentation domains; nothing resolves on a real network.
set -euo pipefail
: "${COLLECTOR_URL:=https://collector.cortexsim-canary.invalid/email/events}"
# (A) EMAIL — permitted click to the AiTM look-alike domain (Proofpoint TAP shape).
python3 -m scripts.eal_simulator.cli run /tmp/email-005-click.yml --live
# (B) IDENTITY — token-replay sign-in from a new ASN (Entra ID sign-in shape).
python3 -m scripts.eal_simulator.cli run /tmp/email-005-replay.yml --live
# (C) COLLECTION — post-compromise the operator logs on to the mailbox and
#     searches finance-related mail for payment-fraud opportunities (Unit 42).
#     Emitted inline as a synthetic Microsoft 365 mailbox-audit record
#     (MailItemsAccessed) to the same collector.
curl -s --max-time 10 -X POST "${COLLECTOR_URL}" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"workload":"Exchange","operation":"MailItemsAccessed","folder":"Inbox","search_terms":"invoice payment wire"}' >/dev/null || true
echo '[CortexSim] SIM-EMAIL-005 AiTM ATO chain emitted.'

input_variables.name: COLLECTOR_URL
input_variables.description: Authorized log-collector endpoint already wired into Cortex XSIAM as a Proofpoint TAP / Microsoft 365 third-party source.

expected_artifacts.description: A permitted click to an AiTM look-alike domain for the target mailbox in the Proofpoint TAP feed.
A successful Entra sign-in whose MFA requirement is satisfied by a token claim (no interactive prompt) from a new ASN — the same user shows a second, non-baseline ASN within the window.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: auth_outcome = "SUCCESS" and auth_status_detail contains "satisfied by claim in the token" and distinct_asns >= 2

expected_artifacts.description: Post-compromise mailbox access on the same user_principal in the Microsoft 365 audit — the operator logs on and searches finance-related mail for payment fraud.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: workload = "Exchange" and operation = "MailItemsAccessed" for the compromised user_principal

iocs.context: AiTM look-alike domain hosting the EvilProxy/Evilginx2 reverse-proxy Microsoft 365 login (Unit 42). Tokenized lure paths (e.g. /HMxVQmxZ) sit under login. subdomains. Appears in the Proofpoint TAP url / M365 Url field.
MitM phishing page targeting Microsoft 365 (Unit 42, Fig. 9 caption). A reverse-proxy look-alike login domain; appears in the Proofpoint TAP url / M365 Url field.

Tokenized AiTM lure URL Advanced URL Filtering began blocking as early as September 2021 (Unit 42). The per-victim token path defeats content-based phish detection. This is the clicked link in the Proofpoint TAP clicksPermitted event.

xql_queries.name: EMAIL-005 AiTM Look-Alike Click Permitted
xql_queries.query:
dataset = proofpoint_tap_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter messageType = "clicksPermitted" and classification = "credphish"
| filter url contains "mcrsfts-passwdupdate.com" or url contains "microsoftonlinesupport.cf"
| comp count() as permitted_clicks, values(url) as aitm_urls, values(senderIP) as sender_ips by recipient
| filter permitted_clicks >= 1
| fields recipient, aitm_urls, sender_ips, permitted_clicks

xql_queries.name: EMAIL-005 Session-Cookie Replay Sign-In from New ASN
xql_queries.query:
dataset = msft_azure_ad_signin
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter auth_outcome = "SUCCESS"
| filter auth_status_detail contains "satisfied by claim in the token"
| comp count() as replayed_signins, count_distinct(src_asn) as distinct_asns, values(src_asn) as sign_in_asns, values(src_geo_country) as countries by user_name
| filter replayed_signins >= 1 and distinct_asns >= 2
| fields user_name, sign_in_asns, countries, distinct_asns, replayed_signins

xql_queries.name: EMAIL-005 Compromised-Mailbox Finance-Mail Reconnaissance
xql_queries.query:
dataset = msft_o365
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter workload = "Exchange" and operation in ("MailItemsAccessed", "MessageBind", "SearchQueryInitiatedExchange")
| comp count() as mailbox_access_events, values(operation) as ops by user_id, client_ip
| filter mailbox_access_events >= 1
| fields user_id, client_ip, ops, mailbox_access_events

correlation_rules.name: AiTM Session-Token Theft to Mailbox-Reconnaissance ATO — Cross-Source Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: XQL(EMAIL-005 AiTM Look-Alike Click Permitted) FOLLOWED_BY XQL(EMAIL-005 Session-Cookie Replay Sign-In from New ASN) FOLLOWED_BY XQL(EMAIL-005 Compromised-Mailbox Finance-Mail Reconnaissance) — joined on user_principal within a 60-minute window. The permitted click to an AiTM look-alike domain plus the token-replay sign-in from a new ASN name the Meddler-in-the-Middle compromise; fusing them with post-compromise finance-mail reconnaissance on the same mailbox raises ONE account-takeover incident. The mailbox-access events are routine activity in isolation, so it is their co-occurrence with the AiTM click and the new-ASN token-replay sign-in on the same user_principal that classifies the takeover. The AiTM domain and the anomalous ASN attach as incident evidence.

products.evidence_query: dataset = msft_azure_ad_signin | filter auth_outcome = "SUCCESS" and auth_status_detail contains "satisfied by claim in the token" | comp count() as replays, count_distinct(src_asn) as distinct_asns, values(src_asn) as asns by user_name | filter replays >= 1 and distinct_asns >= 2

Correlation CR-EMAIL-0005 fuses the AiTM permitted click, the new-ASN token-replay sign-in, and the post-compromise finance-mail reconnaissance on the same user_principal into one account-takeover incident.
On CR-EMAIL-0005 the ATO playbook revokes the user's sessions, forces a phishing-resistant MFA re-registration, and hunts the compromised mailbox for finance-mail access from the anomalous session.

threat_scenarios.name: AiTM Session-Token Theft to Account-Takeover — Cross-Source Correlation
threat_scenarios.description: Prove Cortex XSIAM fuses the low-signal legs of a Meddler-in-the-Middle account takeover — an AiTM permitted click, a token-replay sign-in from a new ASN, and post-compromise finance-mail reconnaissance on the mailbox — into a single incident keyed on user_principal, where each leg alone would not raise an actionable alert.

threat_steps.objective: The AiTM permitted click and the token-replay sign-in are each observable in their source datasets.
preconditions: Cortex XSIAM ingesting proofpoint_tap_raw and msft_azure_ad_signin datasets.
email_emitter and idp_signin_emulator authorized against the lab collector.
steps: Observe the permitted click and the token-replay sign-in for the target user_principal.
success_criteria: XQL `EMAIL-005 AiTM Look-Alike Click Permitted` returns >= 1 row.
XQL `EMAIL-005 Session-Cookie Replay Sign-In from New ASN` returns >= 1 row.

threat_steps.objective: The post-compromise finance-mail reconnaissance leg is observable in the Microsoft 365 audit.
preconditions: Cortex XSIAM ingesting the msft_o365 unified/Entra audit dataset.
steps: Observe the MailItemsAccessed audit records for the same user_principal.
success_criteria: XQL `EMAIL-005 Compromised-Mailbox Finance-Mail Reconnaissance` returns >= 1 row.

threat_steps.objective: All three legs stitch into one account-takeover incident on user_principal.
preconditions: All three EMAIL-005 XQL legs return rows for the same user_principal within the window.
steps: Observe a single stitched account-takeover incident in the Cortex console.
success_criteria: Correlation `CR-EMAIL-0005` raises exactly one incident grouping the AiTM click, the new-ASN token-replay sign-in, and the finance-mail reconnaissance leg on the same user_principal.

preventive_controls: Deploy phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2 / WebAuthn hardware keys) so a proxied login cannot be relayed and no replayable OTP exists.
Enforce Entra Conditional Access with token-protection / sign-in risk policies and compliant-device requirements so a replayed cookie from a new ASN is challenged or blocked.
Revoke refresh/session tokens and force re-authentication on sign-in-risk events so a stolen cookie cannot be reused past the risk signal.
detection_engineering: Alert on Entra sign-ins whose MFA requirement is 'satisfied by a claim in the token' from an ASN outside the user's baseline (a new/second ASN within the window) — the token-replay signature (standard Microsoft 365 / Entra detection engineering).
Alert on anomalous mailbox access (MailItemsAccessed / mailbox search) shortly after a risky sign-in, especially finance-keyword reconnaissance from a session on a non-baseline ASN.

Correlate the AiTM permitted click, the new-ASN token-replay sign-in, and the post-compromise mailbox reconnaissance on a single user_principal within one incident window rather than triaging each in isolation.

changelog.author: Henry Reed
changelog.change: Replace research-intake scaffold with real AiTM/Meddler-in-the-Middle account-takeover detection: per-source XQL legs (AiTM click / token-replay sign-in / post-compromise mailbox activity) stitched by CR-EMAIL-0005 on user_principal, grounded in Unit 42 meddler-phishing reporting. Fills GAP EMAIL as a correlation-terminal F2 card.

changelog.author: Henry Reed
changelog.change: Source-fidelity + XQL repair. (1) Removed the SilverTerrier / Nigerian-BEC actor attribution, tag, and 'SilverTerrier-style' phrasing — the Unit 42 source names no actor. (2) Dropped the unsupported inbox-rule (T1114.003) and device-registration (T1098.005) legs the source never describes; leg C reframed to the behavior the source states — manual logon and finance-mail reconnaissance on the compromised mailbox (T1114.002, MailItemsAccessed). (3) Corrected the microsoftonlinesupport.cf IOC context to a MitM phishing page (Unit 42, Fig. 9) and removed the invented exfil/ForwardTo role and finance-ap@ forwarding address. (4) Attributed the Entra 'satisfied by a claim in the token' sign-in signature to SRC-MICROSOFT-365-DOCS, not Unit 42. (5) Reconciled the msft_azure_ad_signin field vocabulary to the corpus (auth_outcome/src_geo_country/auth_status_detail/src_asn/user_name) and implemented real new-ASN semantics (distinct_asns >= 2) so the leg is not satisfied by routine SSO. Techniques now T1566.002 / T1557 / T1539 / T1550.004 / T1114.002.
